newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 4.

text.p: A man was bashed, set on fire then left for dead in a Stokes Valley park where he lay for more than eight hours before being found, police said on Sunday. Page 1.

Air New Zealand says it will have no difficulty meeting new rudder inspection procedures required by the makers of its Boeing 737-200 aircraft. The airline was responding to Boeing Company's announcement recommending that all 737 jetliners, the world's most widely used passenger planes, be tested within 10 days for potential safety problems in the rudder systems. Page 2.

Prostitution should be used in promoting New Zealand as a travel destination, according to a paper prepared for the Pacific Rim Tourism 2000 conference which opened in Rotorua on Sunday. Sex tourism is already worth at least $15 million to New Zealand's economy, Jody Hanson of Waikato University's education studies department said in the paper. Page 2.
Alliance MPs are paying the equivalent of Alliance tax rates on their salary as a donation to the running of the party organisation. Page 2.

Palmerston North brushmaker Artel Industries has cemented its presence in the South Australian brushware market with two acquisitions that will merge into one manufacturing operation. The move is part of Artel's plan to become an exporter to international markets from Australia and New Zealand. Page 13.

Larger loan books are the main factor driving up registered bank and finance company profitability, even though all banks except Westpac have suffered a fall in interest margins, according to a KPMG survey for the first half of 1996. Page 13.

HongKongBank was not the mystery buyer that had acquired preference shares in Westpac Bank, HongKongBank chief executive David Eldon said. Eldon said HongKongBank, the largest bank in Hong Kong and one of the largest in Asia, would be interested in bank acquisitions in Australia or New Zealand, but only if the price was right. The bank was rumoured to have been the
purchaser of a large block of Westpac Australia shares last week. Westpac Australia owns Westpac in New Zealand and Trust Bank. Page 14.
Specialist property investor Asian Properties reported a $1.4 million after-tax profit in the six months to September 30, down 33.7 percent from the $2.1 million reported last year. Page 14.
St Lukes Group was likely to approach the market for more capital next year if it expanded its $90 million Glenfield Shopping Centre, the shopping mall owner said. Page 14.

Furniture maker Damba will close its Wellington manufacturing plant at the end of the month. The Malaysian-controlled, listed company made $189,000 in the June half-year, down almost three percent on the same period last year. Page 14.

Bay of Plenty Electricity's investment in the Bay Milk co-generation plant has helped push the company's interim profit to $4.03 million. The result for the six months to September 30 reported on Friday is 14 percent higher than the $3.54 milliion reported a year ago. Page 14.

Radio Pacific expects John Banks to turn his back on Parliament if the pressures of being an MP interfere with his job behind the microphone. The MP for Whangarei on Sunday refused to discuss his new position as breakfast show host.

The number of addicted gamblers needed urgent help is rapidly rising, a confidential report reveals. The hard-hitting report, written for a Government-initiated committee on problem gambling by the northern regional health authority North Health, has been kept strictly out of public hands.

Fletcher Homes latest effort to tackle complaints about allegedly overpriced houses has left some homeowners sceptical about a fast solution. Fletcher Homes wrote to complainants telling them they would know before the end of the year whether
their complaints would go to alternative dispute resolution, including mediation.
